# Multi-Rate Audio Core — Implementation Plan

**Status:** detailed plan (companion to `multirate-core-evaluation.md`)
**Scope:** run the emulation core's audio at 44100 / 48000 / 88200 / 96000 / 176400 / 192000 Hz
**Verification cornerstone:** every coefficient table below was produced by a generator that reproduces both shipped 44.1 kHz tables **bit-exactly** (validated 2026-08-17), so these numbers are authoritative, not approximations.

---

## 1. Phases (each independently gated: build clean → new tests green → full suite green)

| # | Change | Files | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Character-chain τ conversion + `MAX_DELAY` 512→1024 (**fixes a live overflow bug** at ≥176.4k and rate-dependent punch character) | `audio_character_chain.h/.cpp` | low |
| 2 | Runtime FIR designer (Kaiser + Hamming windowed-sinc, DC-normalized) + test asserting bit-match to both shipped tables | new `common/sound/filters/fir_designer.h` | low |
| 3 | `FilterDecimator`: phase step parametric (`218750/coreRate`); coefficients from the designer (reference Fc=20 kHz for all rates; optional extended tables for 96/192k) | `filter_decimator.h` | low |
| 4 | `FilterUnreal`: per-rate coefficients from the designer at absolute fc = 11 025 Hz, fs = coreRate×64 | `filter_unreal.h/.cpp` | low |
| 5 | Buffer ceilings: `MAX_SAMPLES_PER_FRAME` → rate-aware (8192 ceiling), ring/device buffers follow; audit `PSG_CLOCKS_PER_AUDIO_SAMPLE` consumers | `audio.h`, `soundmanager.h`, client soundmanagers | medium (touches sizes everywhere) |
| 6 | `CoreRate` config parameter (`[SOUND] CoreRate=auto\|44100\|...\|192000`, `auto` = device family); plumb through `SoundManager`/`Beeper`/AY ctors; changing it triggers full sound reset | `config.cpp/.h`, `soundmanager.cpp`, chip ctors | medium |
| 7 | Rate-matrix tests: accumulator exactness per rate (periods from §D), pipeline counts, **FFT pitch invariance** (a generated AY tone must measure the same Hz at every core rate via `AudioHelper::detectBaseFrequencyFFT`) | `sound_adaptivity_test.cpp` + new | low |

Ordering rationale: phase 1 is a standalone bug fix; 2 unlocks 3–4; 5–6 are
the plumbing; 7 is the acceptance harness. DRC (already shipped) needs no
change — its base ratio `device/core` already handles every pairing.

## 1a. Architecture principles (elegance & flexibility contract)

1. **One rate parameter, one flow direction.** `coreRate` enters at exactly
   one point (`SoundManager` construction, sourced from config) and flows
   down through constructors: `SoundManager(rate)` → `Beeper(rate)` /
   `SoundChip_TurboSound(rate)` / `Covox(rate)` → filters. No component
   reads a global rate constant; no component owns a second copy.
2. **Filters are rate-constructed, not rate-hardcoded.** Each filter takes
   its rates in the constructor and designs itself via the runtime designer:
   `FilterDecimator(outputRate, Bandwidth::Reference|Extended)`,
   `UnrealFilter(coreRate)`. Adding a new rate (e.g. a future 384 kHz)
   requires zero new tables and zero code changes — only widening the
   validation matrix.
3. **The per-rate tables in this document are validation artifacts, not
   code.** They pin the designer's output for audit and regression (a unit
   test asserts the designer reproduces the shipped 44.1k tables bit-exactly
   and spot-checks the other rates against these tables). The only baked
   numbers left in the codebase are the two shipped tables, retained inside
   the designer's unit test as golden references.
4. **Character is specified in physical units.** Cutoffs in Hz, envelope
   times in seconds, delays in seconds — per-sample coefficients are always
   derived at construction, never stored as magic numbers. This is what
   makes "same sound at every rate" a structural property instead of a
   maintenance promise.
5. **No hot-switching complexity.** Rate changes rebuild the sound stack
   through the ordinary reset path; nothing is dynamically re-coefficiented
   mid-stream.

## 2. The runtime designer (replaces all baked tables)

```cpp
// Windowed-sinc lowpass, DC-normalized (sum == 1). Reproduces the shipped
// 44.1k tables bit-exactly:
//   FilterDecimator: designFir(96,  20000, 218750,  Window::Kaiser, 5.0)
//   FilterUnreal:    designFir(128, 11025, 2822400, Window::Hamming)
std::vector<double> designFir(size_t taps, double fc, double fs, Window w, double beta = 0.0);
```

Kaiser needs I₀ (series expansion, ~20 terms); Hamming is `0.54 − 0.46·cos(2πn/M)`.
Cost: microseconds at init. The static tables below remain in this document
as the audit reference and as a fallback if baked tables are ever preferred.

## 2a. Quality tiers (the "topmost quality" requirement)

Per-path quality at the target rates:

- **Beeper/Covox/tape (blip_buf):** rate-independent by construction — steps
  are placed at T-state resolution and rendered band-limited at any output
  rate. Quality *improves* with rate (passband extends toward the higher
  Nyquist). Nothing to do beyond buffer ceilings.
- **AY HQ path:** generation at 218.75 kHz already exceeds every target
  rate's Nyquist; the only quality bound is the decimation FIR. The shipped
  96-tap Kaiser **β=5 ≈ 56 dB** stopband — the deliberate "shipped
  character", not hi-fi-topmost. Since the runtime designer makes tap count
  and β plain parameters, define two tiers:

  | Tier | Design | Stopband | Purpose |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `Reference` | 96 taps, β=5 | ~56 dB | Bit-compatible with shipped sound |
  | `HighFidelity` | 192 taps, β=9 | ~90+ dB | Topmost: transparent decimation at all rates |

  CPU cost of HighFidelity is negligible (the FIR runs per *output* sample;
  at gentler high-rate ratios the per-second work barely grows). Default:
  `Reference` at 44100 (preserves today's output bit-for-bit),
  `HighFidelity` elsewhere — configurable.
- **AY legacy path (`FilterUnreal`):** intentionally characterful (Hamming,
  ~53 dB) — it exists to sound like Unreal Speccy, not to be transparent.
  The HQ path is the quality path; the legacy path gets per-rate tables for
  character parity only.
- **Final stage:** with core rate == device native rate the DRC is a
  bit-exact bypass (pure ±0.5% trim territory); the Hermite stage's
  interpolation error near unity is below −90 dBFS.

## 3. Decisions locked in (from the evaluation)

- `FilterUnreal` fc is **absolute** (11 025 Hz) at every rate — preserves the
  shipped tonal character. (fc = rate/4 would make one table serve all rates
  but brightens the tone with rate; rejected.)
- `FilterDecimator` keeps Fc = 20 kHz at every rate by default (identical
  character; coefficients rate-invariant since the input side is fixed at
  218.75 kHz — only the phase step changes). Extended-bandwidth tables are
  opt-in for archival capture at 96/192k.
- Envelope character is defined by **time constants**, not per-sample
  coefficients: `alpha = 1 − exp(−1/(τ·fs))`, `decay = exp(−1/(τ·fs))`.

### A2. HighFidelity tier tables — 192-tap Kaiser β=9 (~90+ dB stopband), input fixed 218 750 Hz

Like the Reference tier, coefficients depend only on cutoff, NOT on output
rate (the FIR operates at the fixed 218.75 kHz input side). Three cutoffs
cover the whole rate matrix:

| Table | Fc | Valid output rates | Stopband starts ≈ |
|---|---|---|---|
| HF_REFERENCE | 20 kHz | all (default character) | ~22 kHz |
| HF_EXT_40K | 40 kHz | 88200, 96000 (extended BW) | ~43 kHz |
| HF_EXT_80K | 80 kHz | 176400, 192000 (extended BW) | ~83 kHz |

### B. FilterUnreal (legacy AY path) — 128-tap Hamming, fs = coreRate × 64, fc = 11 025 Hz absolute

Absolute cutoff preserves the shipped tonal character at every core rate.
(The alternative — fc = rate/4, the shipped ratio — makes the table rate-invariant
but brightens the tone as the rate rises; rejected to keep A/B parity.)

### C. AudioCharacterChain — punch and room at every rate (complete)

The chain has FOUR rate dependencies; only the envelope taus were obvious.

**C.1 Punch first-difference normalization (the critical one).** Both punch
terms are built on `diff = x[n] - x[n-1]`, a differentiator whose gain is
`2*sin(pi*f/fs)` - it halves per octave of sample rate. Uncorrected, the
edge tilt shrinks linearly with fs and the transient boost (diff x
envelope-of-|diff|) shrinks QUADRATICALLY: at 192 kHz the punch would nearly
vanish. Fix (one line, keeps every shipped parameter value valid at every
rate):

```cpp
const float diffNorm = static_cast<float>(_sampleRate) / 44100.0f;  // At setup()
...
float diffL = (outL - _prevOutL) * _diffNorm;   // Normalized difference
float diffR = (outR - _prevOutR) * _diffNorm;
// edgeBlend / transBoost / envelope all consume the normalized diff unchanged
```

Accuracy of the normalization vs the shipped 44.1k response: exact in the
bass/mid band; at 15 kHz the tilt is +0.28 dB (48k) / +1.37 dB (96k) /
+1.63 dB (192k) brighter - because the linearized differentiator is actually
the more faithful +6 dB/oct; the shipped 44.1k version sags approaching its
Nyquist. Documented as acceptable (and arguably an improvement); an exact
match would need a compensating pole and is not worth the complexity.

**C.2 Room one-pole damping.** `_roomLpCoef = 0.7` corresponds to an
8 450 Hz cutoff only at 44.1k. Store the cutoff, derive alpha per rate:
`alpha = 1 - exp(-2*pi*fc/fs)`:

| Rate | 44100 | 48000 | 88200 | 96000 | 176400 | 192000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| roomLpCoef (fc = 8450 Hz) | 0.700000 | 0.669170 | 0.452277 | 0.424822 | 0.259917 | 0.241595 |

(The AY room preset uses alpha = 1.0 = no damping - rate-invariant as-is.)

**C.3 Delays** are already seconds-based (`0.003*fs`, `0.002*fs`);
`MAX_DELAY` rises 512 -> **1024** (0.003 x 192000 = 576; live overflow bug).

**C.4 Envelope coefficients.** Shipped per-sample values are only correct at
44 100 Hz. Convert to time constants (tau) and recompute per rate:
`alpha = 1 - exp(-1/(tau*fs))` for attack-style EMAs,
`coeff = exp(-1/(tau*fs))` for release-style decays. (With the C.1
normalization, the envelope input |diff| is also rate-invariant, so
`transBoost` needs no separate correction.)

| Parameter | Shipped @44.1k | tau | 44100 | 48000 | 88200 | 96000 | 176400 | 192000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| attack (EMA alpha) | 0.3 | 63.6 µs | 0.300000 | 0.279417 | 0.163340 | 0.151129 | 0.085309 | 0.078658 |
| release (beeper) | 0.998 | 11.33 ms | 0.998000 | 0.998162 | 0.998999 | 0.999081 | 0.999500 | 0.999540 |
| release (AY) | 0.9995 | 45.34 ms | 0.999500 | 0.999541 | 0.999750 | 0.999770 | 0.999875 | 0.999885 |

Delay-line lengths: `baseDelay = 0.003*fs`, `ayDelay = 0.002*fs` (already
rate-relative); `MAX_DELAY` must rise from 512 to **1024** (0.003 x 192000 = 576).

### D. Per-rate frame geometry (integer sample accumulator handles all exactly)

| Core rate | Pentagon samples/frame | period | ZX48/128 samples/frame | period | MAX_SAMPLES_PER_FRAME needed (2x multiplier) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 44100 | 903.1680 | 125 frames | 880.5888 | 625 frames | 1807 |
| 48000 | 983.0400 | 25 frames | 958.4640 | 125 frames | 1967 |
| 88200 | 1806.3360 | 125 frames | 1761.1776 | 625 frames | 3613 |
| 96000 | 1966.0800 | 25 frames | 1916.9280 | 125 frames | 3933 |
| 176400 | 3612.6720 | 125 frames | 3522.3552 | 625 frames | 7226 |
| 192000 | 3932.1600 | 25 frames | 3833.8560 | 125 frames | 7865 |

Buffer ceiling for all supported rates: **8192 stereo frames** per frame buffer
(192 kHz x 2x multiplier = 7865). Ring buffer scales to 8x that (as today's ratio).
